title: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA): The Ocular Perspective
summary: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (formerly Wegener’s) is a systemic necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis primarily affecting small-to-medium vessels. Ocular involvement occurs in up to 50% of patients and is often the presenting sign, necessitating a multidisciplinary approach.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: GPA is a systemic pauci-immune vasculitis associated with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA). It manifests as necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, typically involving the upper and lower respiratory tracts and kidneys. Ocular pathology stems from direct vasculitis or contiguous spread from orbital granulomatous tissue.

sections.title: Red Flags: Ocular Emergencies
content: Peripheral Ulcerative Keratitis (PUK) - high risk of globe perforation
Rapidly progressive orbital mass causing compressive optic neuropathy
Sudden vision loss from retinal artery or vein occlusion
Acute scleritis unresponsive to topical steroids

rows: Upper/lower respiratory tract, eye involvement, no systemic signs
Renal failure (Cr > 5.6 mg/dL) or other end-organ failure

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 2: Biopsy (Gold Standard: Tissue biopsy from lung/sinus/sclera)
Step 3: Imaging (CT Orbit/Sinus for bony erosion; MRI for soft tissue)
Step 4: Chest X-ray/CT Chest to assess pulmonary nodules
Step 5: Urinalysis & Creatinine to assess renal involvement

sections.title: Treatment Protocol
content: Induction: Cyclophosphamide (oral or IV pulse) + High dose IV Methylprednisolone (1g/day x 3 days) followed by tapered oral Prednisone.
Biologics: Rituximab is non-inferior to Cyclophosphamide for induction, especially in relapsing disease.
Ocular Surgery: Defer surgery if possible; perform only once inflammation is controlled due to poor wound healing (scleral patch grafts for PUK).
Recent Advances: Landmark RAVE (Rituximab in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis) trial established Rituximab as the preferred agent for induction in severe cases.
